memories.memory: I was diagnosed with high blood pressure in 2022 after a routine checkup showed readings around 165/95, and I now take amlodipine every morning.
Years of kneeling and lifting at work left me with recurring pain in my right knee, especially after long shifts or heavy squats at the gym.
In September 2023, I tore the meniscus in my left knee during a veterans' football match and completed eight weeks of physiotherapy instead of having surgery.
My doctor told me last winter that my blood sugar was in the prediabetic range, so I have been cutting back on sweet pastries and checking my weight every Sunday.
I have mild hearing loss in my left ear from working around grinders and compressors, but I still put off getting a hearing aid because I dislike wearing one on the job.
For several months after my wife's illness in 2021, I had trouble sleeping and used a short course of prescribed sleeping tablets before returning to a regular exercise routine.
A workplace accident in 2018 left me with a small piece of metal in my right forearm, and the surgeon advised leaving it in place because removing it could damage a nerve.
